claim: Enhancers are regulatory elements enriched for H3K4me1 and H3K27ac histone modifications.
source: Enhancers demonstrate unique epigenetic markings, enriched for H3K4me1 and H3K27ac (Creyghton et al., 2010; Heintzman et al., 2007; Rada-Iglesias et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Creyghton et al., 2010; Heintzman et al., 2007; Rada-Iglesias et al., 2011).

claim: Enhancers are highly accessible as demonstrated by elevated DNase sensitivity and transposition susceptibility.
source: and are highly accessible, as demonstrated by elevated DNase sensitivity and transposition susceptibility (Boyle et al., 2008; Buenrostro et al., 2013; Thurman et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Boyle et al., 2008; Buenrostro et al., 2013; Thurman et al., 2012).

claim: Greater than 300,000 enhancers are predicted to be encoded in the human genome.
source: it is now predicted that greater than 300,000 enhancers are encoded in the human genome (ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012; Zhu et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012; Zhu et al., 2013).

claim: Chromosomes occupy discrete chromosomal territories within the nucleus.
source: Within the nucleus, each chromosome occupies discrete chromosomal territories (Cremer et al., 2006)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Cremer et al., 2006).

claim: Chromosomal territories are structured into distinct compartments that separate active and repressive chromatin.
source: These territories are further structured into distinct compartments that separate active and repressive chromatin (Lieberman-Aiden et al., 2009; Sexton et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Lieberman-Aiden et al., 2009; Sexton et al., 2012).

claim: Chromosomes are partitioned into sub-megabase sized topologically-associated domains (TADs).
source: At finer scales, chromosomes are partitioned into largely-invariant, sub-megabase sized topologically-associated domains (TADs), which break up the linear genome into interactive neighborhoods (Dixon et al., 2012; Nora et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Dixon et al., 2012; Nora et al., 2012).

claim: Chromosomal contacts are disfavored across TAD boundaries.
source: Chromosomal contacts are disfavored across TAD boundaries.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the text based on established knowledge about TAD structure.

claim: Disruption of TAD architecture leads to dysregulation of gene expression.
source: and disruption of TAD architecture leads to dysregulation of gene expression (Dowen et al., 2014; Gröschel et al., 2014; Guo et al., 2015; Lupiáñez et al., 2015; Narendra et al., 2015; Nora et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Dowen et al., 2014; Gröschel et al., 2014; Guo et al., 2015; Lupiáñez et al., 2015; Narendra et al., 2015; Nora et al., 2017).

claim: Sox2 is a high-mobility group DNA-binding transcription factor with important roles in embryonic development.
source: Sox2 encodes a high-mobility group (HMG) DNA-binding transcription factor with important roles in embryonic development (Kamachi and Kondoh, 2013; Lefebvre et al., 2007; Sarkar and Hochedlinger, 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Kamachi and Kondoh, 2013; Lefebvre et al., 2007; Sarkar and Hochedlinger, 2013).

claim: Sox2 functions as an essential regulator of pluripotency in embryonic stem cells.
source: Sox2 also functions as an essential regulator of pluripotency, where it cooperates with other transcriptional regulators to maintain the pluripotency transcriptional program and keep embryonic stem cells in the undifferentiated state (Chen et al., 2008a; Young, 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Chen et al., 2008a; Young, 2011).

claim: Sox2 expression in mouse ESCs is controlled by a single, strong distal enhancer called the Sox2 Control Region (SCR).
source: However, Sox2 expression in mouse ESCs is controlled by a single, strong distal enhancer called the Sox2 Control Region (Li et al., 2014; Zhou et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Li et al., 2014; Zhou et al., 2014).

claim: Genetic ablation of SCR in ESCs leads to loss of Sox2 expression in cis.
source: Genetic ablation of SCR in ESCs leads to loss of Sox2 expression in cis.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the text based on experimental observations.

claim: SCR is sufficient for Sox2 regulation in ESCs.
source: Moreover, SCR maintains Sox2 expression levels in the context of compound deletion of alternative Sox2 enhancers, suggesting SCR is sufficient for Sox2 regulation in ESCs (Zhou et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Zhou et al., 2014).

claim: Publicly available 4C and HiC datasets reveal enriched contacts between SCR and the Sox2 promoter region.
source: Publicly available circularized chromosome conformation capture (4C) and HiC datasets reveal enriched contacts between SCR and the Sox2 promoter region, suggesting that these enhancer-promoter interactions may play an important role in SCR function (Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to publicly available datasets and visualization in Figure 1B.

claim: The textbook model proposes that enhancers influence target gene promoters through protein-protein complexes and physical interaction mediated by a DNA loop.
source: The textbook model proposes that enhancers influence target gene promoters through protein-protein complexes and physical interaction mediated by a DNA loop (Alberts et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a textbook (Alberts et al., 2014).

claim: 3C-based studies have identified enriched contacts between enhancer and promoter elements.
source: Experimental support for this model comes primarily from numerous chromosome conformation capture (3C)-based studies that have identified enriched contacts between enhancer and promoter elements (Jin et al., 2013; Li et al., 2012; Rao et al., 2014; Sanyal et al., 2012; Weintraub et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Jin et al., 2013; Li et al., 2012; Rao et al., 2014; Sanyal et al., 2012; Weintraub et al., 2017).

claim: Driving contacts between an enhancer-promoter pair is sufficient to augment gene expression.
source: and recent observations that driving contacts between an enhancer-promoter pair is sufficient to augment gene expression (Bartman et al., 2016; Deng et al., 2012; Deng et al., 2014; Morgan et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Bartman et al., 2016; Deng et al., 2012; Deng et al., 2014; Morgan et al., 2017).

claim: Sonic hedgehog (Shh) enhancers that drive expression in the brain move further, rather than closer, to the Shh gene when activated.
source: For example, sonic hedgehog (Shh) enhancers that drive expression in the brain move further, rather than closer, to the Shh gene when activated (Benabdallah et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Benabdallah et al., 2017).

claim: In Drosophila, coupled reporter genes regulated by a shared enhancer show coordinated transcriptional bursting.
source: Furthermore, in Drosophila, coupled reporter genes regulated by a shared enhancer nevertheless show coordinated transcriptional bursting, suggesting either that an enhancer can contact multiple genes at once or that contact can be decoupled from transcription (Fukaya et al., 2016; Lim et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Fukaya et al., 2016; Lim et al., 2018).

claim: Super enhancers are clusters of enhancers highly enriched for coactivators like Mediator and BRD4.
source: Super enhancers -- clusters of enhancers that are highly enriched for coactivators like Mediator and BRD4 (Lovén et al., 2013; Whyte et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Lovén et al., 2013; Whyte et al., 2013).

claim: Super enhancers have been proposed to activate transcription through nucleation of activator droplets.
source: -- have been proposed to activate transcription through nucleation of activator droplets rather than stepwise assembly of transcription complexes (Hnisz et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Hnisz et al., 2017).

claim: Recent imaging has provided support for the idea that super enhancers activate transcription through nucleation of activator droplets.
source: and recent imaging has provided support for this idea (Cho et al., 2018; Sabari et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Cho et al., 2018; Sabari et al., 2018).

claim: A two-step genetic engineering strategy with bacteriophage integrases was used to target repetitive arrays to the mouse genome.
source: We opted to target these arrays to the mouse genome using a two-step genetic engineering strategy with bacteriophage integrases for two reasons (Figure 1A, see Supplementary file 1 for protocol).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Repetitive sequences can be unstable during vector construction.
source: First, repetitive sequences can be unstable during vector construction, making it advantageous to use generic targeting vectors portable between genomic loci.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the experimental approach based on established knowledge.

claim: 129/Cast F1 hybrid ESCs were used to target two regions on the same chromosome.
source: To target two regions on the same chromosome, we used 129/Cast F1 hybrid ESCs, derived from crossing the 129 mouse strain to the divergent subspecies Mus musculus castaneus.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design.

claim: Genetic polymorphisms between 129 and Cast genomes were used to design allele-specific CRISPR guide RNAs.
source: This allowed us to limit editing to the 129 allele by using genetic polymorphisms between the two parental genomes to design allele-specific CRISPR guide RNAs.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design.

claim: The cuO array was inserted 8 kb centromeric to the Sox2 TSS in the Sox2-SCR cell line.
source: Sox2-8CcuO/+; Sox2-117TtetO/+ (Sox2-SCR) ESCs were used to track Sox2/SCR location.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1B showing the location of the cuO array.

claim: The tetO array was inserted approximately 5 kb telomeric to the SCR boundary (117 kb telomeric to Sox2 TSS) in the Sox2-SCR cell line.
source: Sox2-8CcuO/+; Sox2-117TtetO/+ (Sox2-SCR) ESCs were used to track Sox2/SCR location.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1B showing the location of the tetO array.

claim: The Sox2 expression ratio (129/Cast) was similar for modified cell lines compared to parental ESCs.
source: We detected a similar Sox2 expression ratio (129/Cast) using an allele-specific qPCR assay for modified cell lines compared to the parental ESCs, suggesting Sox2 regulation is intact despite genetic alteration of the locus (Analysis of Variance, p=0.215, Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 with statistical analysis (ANOVA, p=0.215).

claim: Insertion of the cuO and tetO arrays within the Sox2 locus did not disrupt Sox2-SCR contacts on the modified allele.
source: Furthermore, we found insertion of the cuO and tetO arrays within the Sox2 locus did not disrupt Sox2-SCR contacts on the modified allele (Figure 1—figure supplement 3)
evidence: The claim is supported by 4C data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The majority of ESCs demonstrated a single, bright focus of CymR-GFP and TetR-tdTom in close proximity.
source: 3D time series of proliferating ESCs showed the majority of cells demonstrated a single, bright focus of CymR-GFP and TetR-tdTom in the ESC nucleus in close proximity.
evidence: This is a direct observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Many foci revealed the presence of two juxtaposed sister chromatids.
source: Many of these foci revealed the presence of two juxtaposed sister chromatids (Video 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from live-cell imaging shown in Video 1.

claim: Cells with single, diffraction-limited spots for cuO and tetO likely represent cells in the G1/early S phase of the cell cycle.
source: we excluded these loci from our analysis and focused on cells demonstrating single, diffraction-limited spots for cuO and tetO, likely representing cells in the G1/early S phase of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of single spots versus doublets.

claim: The localization precision in the X, Y, and Z dimensions is estimated to be 12 nm, 10 nm, and 36 nm, respectively, for cuO/CymR.
source: By localization of fluorescent beads at a comparable signal-to-noise ratio, we estimate our localization precision in the X, Y, and Z dimensions to be 12 nm, 10 nm, and 36 nm, respectively, for cuO/CymR
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements using fluorescent beads as described in the methods.

claim: The localization precision in the X, Y, and Z dimensions is estimated to be 16 nm, 16 nm, 50 nm for tetO/TetR.
source: and 16 nm, 16 nm, 50 nm for tetO/TetR (Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements using fluorescent beads shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The uncertainty in measured 3D distance between cuO/CymR and tetO/TetR is between 40–50 nm.
source: These precision estimates translate to an uncertainty in measured 3D distance between cuO/CymR and tetO/TetR of between 40–50 nm (Figure 2—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is calculated from the localization precision estimates and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Distances below 55 nm are dominated by the noise component (i.e. >50% error).
source: This localization uncertainty degrades the accuracy of very small distance measurements; distances below 55 nm are dominated by the noise component (i.e. >50% error, Figure 2—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is calculated from the localization precision estimates and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The Sox2/SCR pair shows a unimodal distance distribution with positive skew.
source: This analysis revealed a unimodal distribution with positive skew (Hartigan's Dip Test for multimodality, p=1).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of the distance measurements (Hartigan's Dip Test, p=1).

claim: On average, Sox2/SCR labels are separated by a few hundred nanometers in the ESC nucleus (mean = 339 nm).
source: On average, Sox2/SCR labels are separated by a few hundred nanometers in the ESC nucleus (mean = 339 nm, Figure 2B)
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the imaging data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 2.1% of Sox2/SCR distance measurements are greater than 750 nm.
source: Infrequently, we observed the Sox2 region adopt an extended conformation, leading to considerable Sox2/SCR separation distance (2.1% of measurements > 750 nm, 0.35% of measurements > 1 µm).
evidence: This is a direct calculation from the imaging data.

claim: 0.35% of Sox2/SCR distance measurements are greater than 1 µm.
source: Infrequently, we observed the Sox2 region adopt an extended conformation, leading to considerable Sox2/SCR separation distance (2.1% of measurements > 750 nm, 0.35% of measurements > 1 µm).
evidence: This is a direct calculation from the imaging data.

claim: The Control-Control pair showed increased separation distance compared to Sox2/SCR.
source: We found that, while one control pair (Control-Control) did show increased separation distance as compared to Sox2/SCR
evidence: This is a direct comparison of the distance measurements between different cell lines.

claim: The SCR-Control pair showed a similar distribution to Sox2/SCR.
source: our other control set (SCR-Control), consisting of the SCR paired with a non-specific partner, showed a similar distribution to Sox2/SCR (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is a direct comparison of the distance distributions shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Control-Control demonstrated significantly increased distances compared to Sox2-SCR.
source: while Control-Control demonstrated significantly increased distances (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison shown in Figure 2D.

claim: There is evidence for a topological boundary, potentially established by the SCR element, separating the two labeled regions in the Control-Control configuration.
source: Reinspection of chromosomal contact maps revealed evidence for a topological boundary, potentially established by the SCR element, separating the two labeled regions in the Control-Control configuration (Figure 1A)
evidence: This is based on analysis of chromosomal contact maps shown in Figure 1A.

claim: SCR does not show greater proximity to the Sox2 gene than to a non-specific control.
source: These results suggest that SCR does not show greater proximity to the Sox2 gene than to a non-specific control.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of Sox2-SCR and SCR-Control distance distributions.

claim: A ~111 kb fragment was deleted between the cuO and tetO labels in the Sox2-SCR configuration, leaving a 14 kb tether between the labels.
source: To this end, we used CRISPR/Cas9 to delete a ~ 111 kb fragment between the cuO and tetO labels in the Sox2-SCR configuration, leaving a 14 kb tether between the labels (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is a direct description of the genetic manipulation performed, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Visualization of the Sox2-del-SCR label configuration in living ESCs demonstrated a significant shift to more proximal distance values.
source: Visualization of this label configuration in living ESCs demonstrated a significant shift to more proximal distance values (Figure 2C,D)
evidence: This is based on imaging data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: A direct Sox2/SCR interaction would be confined to shorter 3D distances than those observed for the Sox2-SCR pair.
source: These results are consistent with our expectation that a direct Sox2/SCR interaction would be confined shorter 3D distances than those observed for the Sox2-SCR pair and validate our experimental capacity to measure these differences.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of Sox2-SCR and Sox2-del-SCR distance distributions.

claim: Sox2-SCR pair shows no unique spatial characteristics in ESCs.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate no unique spatial characteristics for the Sox2-SCR pair in ESCs.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the distance measurements and comparisons with control pairs.

claim: Neural precursor cells (NPCs) maintain Sox2 expression despite inactivation of the SCR.
source: To this end, we derived neural precursor cells (NPCs), a cell-type that maintains Sox2 expression despite inactivation of the SCR and reduced Sox2/SCR contacts by chromosome conformation capture carbon copy (5C) (Figure 3B) (Beagan et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3B and a citation (Beagan et al., 2017).

claim: NPCs show reduced Sox2/SCR contacts by 5C.
source: To this end, we derived neural precursor cells (NPCs), a cell-type that maintains Sox2 expression despite inactivation of the SCR and reduced Sox2/SCR contacts by chromosome conformation capture carbon copy (5C) (Figure 3B) (Beagan et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by a citation (Beagan et al., 2017).

claim: FLK1+/PDGFRα+ mesodermal precursors (MES) downregulate Sox2 expression and inactivate the SCR element.
source: As an additional comparison, we differentiated our ESC lines into FLK1+/PDGFRα+ mesodermal precursors (MES), a cell type which downregulates Sox2 expression and inactivates the SCR element (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All label pairs embedded in the Sox2 locus showed greater proximity in differentiated cells compared to ESCs.
source: Interestingly, we observed that all label pairs embedded in the Sox2 locus showed greater proximity in differentiated cells compared to ESCs (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is based on imaging data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Changes in Sox2 locus proximity were significant when comparing mean distances per cell between label pairs in NPCs or MES with ESCs.
source: These changes were significant when comparing mean distances per cell between label pairs in NPCs or MES with ESCs (Figure 3D)
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The entire Sox2 locus adopts a more compact conformation upon ESC differentiation, regardless of transcriptional status of Sox2.
source: These data suggest the entire Sox2 locus adopts a more compact conformation upon ESC differentiation, regardless of transcriptional status of Sox2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that all label pairs show increased proximity in differentiated cells.

claim: A heterozygous genetic deletion of the SCR element on the 129 allele in ESCs was generated using CRISPR/Cas9.
source: To explore if compaction of the Sox2 locus conformation might be driven by inactivation of the SCR element (which occurs in both NPCs and MES) or could be driven by other factors related to cellular differentiation, we generated a heterozygous genetic deletion of the SCR element on the 129 allele in ESCs using CRISPR/Cas9 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is a direct description of the genetic manipulation performed, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: SCR-deleted ESCs show no signs of differentiation and maintained naive ESC morphology.
source: These cells show no signs of differentiation and maintained naive ESC morphology, consistent with previous studies (Zhou et al., 2014)
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by a citation (Zhou et al., 2014).

claim: SCR deletion led to reduction of Sox2 expression from the cis allele to undetectable levels by qPCR.
source: Moreover, SCR deletion led to reduction of Sox2 expression from the cis allele to undetectable levels by qPCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Live-cell visualization of the cuO and tetO labels in SCR-deleted ESCs demonstrated a slight shift in 3D distances towards greater proximity.
source: Live-cell visualization of the cuO and tetO labels in these cells demonstrated a slight shift in 3D distances towards greater proximity
evidence: This is based on imaging data.

claim: The shift in 3D distances in SCR-deleted ESCs was small compared to that seen after differentiation to NPCs or MES.
source: however, this shift was small compared to that seen after differentiation to NPCs or MES (Figure 3—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is based on comparison of imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Hierarchical clustering analysis revealed that SCR-deleted ESCs were most similar to other ESC lines.
source: Hierarchical clustering analysis of the similarity between distance histograms revealed that SCR-deleted ESCs were most similar to other ESC lines (Figure 3—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is based on hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Sox2 locus organization is significantly altered with ESC differentiation but largely robust to changes in Sox2 or SCR activity.
source: These observations suggest that Sox2 locus organization is significantly altered with ESC differentiation but largely robust to changes in Sox2 or SCR activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of distance measurements in different cell types and conditions.

claim: Striking variation in locus organization was observed between individual cells.
source: While all three label pairs showed comparable distance profiles across the cell population, we observed striking variation in locus organization between individual cells (Figure 4A,B, Video 2)
evidence: This is based on imaging data shown in Figure 4A,B and Video 2.

claim: Label pairs were observed in prolonged compact or extended conformations as well as gradual or sharp transitions between the two.
source: We observed label pairs in prolonged compact or extended conformations as well as gradual or sharp transitions between the two (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is based on imaging data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Few label pairs explored their entire range during the imaging window (~25 min).
source: However, few label pairs explored their entire range – the distance spread observed across our cell population -- during our imaging window (~25 min)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data.

claim: Sox2 locus conformation dynamics are slow over tens of minutes.
source: demonstrating that Sox2 locus conformation dynamics are slow over tens of minutes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that few loci explore their full range during the imaging window.

claim: Relative step sizes for the Sox2-SCR pair were significant (e.g. 180 nm).
source: Both relative step sizes (defined as the 3D displacement of the cuO label between frames if the tetO location is fixed) and the change in 3D separation distance between frames were significant (e.g.180 nm and 79 nm, respectively, for the Sox2-SCR pair, 20 s per frame, Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The change in 3D separation distance between frames for the Sox2-SCR pair was significant (e.g. 79 nm).
source: Both relative step sizes (defined as the 3D displacement of the cuO label between frames if the tetO location is fixed) and the change in 3D separation distance between frames were significant (e.g.180 nm and 79 nm, respectively, for the Sox2-SCR pair, 20 s per frame, Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The autocorrelation function for each label pair revealed a monotonic decay with increasing lag times.
source: Computation of the autocorrelation function for each label pair revealed a monotonic decay with increasing lag times (Figure 4D)
evidence: This is based on autocorrelation analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: An initial rapid reduction in autocorrelation in the small time lag regime was observed, driven by a period of effective local exploration.
source: We observe an initial rapid reduction in autocorrelation in the small time lag regime, driven by a period of effective local exploration.
evidence: This is based on interpretation of the autocorrelation analysis.

claim: At long time lags (>10 mins), the autocorrelation function for both control pairs appears to flatten to a slope of zero.
source: Interestingly, at long time lags (>10 mins), the autocorrelation function for both control pairs appears to flatten to a slope of zero, suggesting that conformational memory for some loci may be quite long-lived.
evidence: This is based on observation of the autocorrelation function shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Conformational memory for some loci may be quite long-lived.
source: Interestingly, at long time lags (>10 mins), the autocorrelation function for both control pairs appears to flatten to a slope of zero, suggesting that conformational memory for some loci may be quite long-lived.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation of the autocorrelation function.

claim: Encounters between loci are highly dependent on the initial configuration of the genomic region.
source: An important implication of this behavior of chromatin is that encounters between loci are highly dependent on the initial configuration of the genomic region (Figure 4E)
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: 73% of Sox2-SCR pairs that start within 200 nm of each other have at least one encounter below 100 nm over the 25 min imaging window.
source: For instance, while 73% of Sox2-SCR pairs that start within 200 nm of each other are observed to have at least one encounter below 100 nm over the 25 min imaging window
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data.

claim: 18% of Sox2-SCR pairs that start greater than 600 nm away have at least one encounter below 100 nm over the 25 min imaging window.
source: this drops to 18% for pairs that start greater than 600 nm away.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data.

claim: Enhancer proximity, and therefore the capacity for direct enhancer-promoter contact, is likely to be highly variable across time within a cell and between cells within a population.
source: Given the observed inertia in locus conformation, enhancer proximity, and therefore the capacity for direct enhancer-promoter contact, is likely to be highly variable across time within a cell and between cells within a population.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation of slow locus dynamics and dependence of encounters on initial configuration.

claim: The endogenous 129 Sox2 allele was replaced with a modified version that includes a P2A-puromycin resistance gene fusion and 24 MS2 stem loops inserted into the 3' UTR of the Sox2 gene.
source: Using CRISPR/Cas9 genome engineering, we replaced the endogenous 129 Sox2 allele with a modified version that includes a P2A-puromycin resistance gene fusion and 24 MS2 stem loops inserted into the 3' UTR of the Sox2 gene (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is a direct description of the genetic manipulation performed, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transcription levels derived from the Sox2-MS2 reporter allele were 35% of those from the untargeted 129 allele.
source: Transcription levels derived from the Sox2-MS2 reporter allele were 35% of those from the untargeted 129 allele (Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Reduced transcription from the Sox2-MS2 reporter allele is potentially due to reduced stability of transcripts labeled with MS2 stem loops.
source: potentially due to reduced stability of transcripts labeled with MS2 stem loops (Ochiai et al., 2014)
evidence: This is a speculation based on a citation to published literature (Ochiai et al., 2014).

claim: Western blotting of Sox2-MS2 lysate revealed a SOX2 doublet, suggesting proper expression of both wild-type SOX2 and the SOX-P2A fusion.
source: Western blotting of Sox2-MS2 lysate revealed a SOX2 doublet as expected, suggesting proper expression of both wild-type SOX2 and the SOX-P2A fusion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on Western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Time-lapse confocal microscopy revealed bright flashes of MS2cp signal in the ESC nucleus, which occurred in spatial proximity to the cuO and tetO labels.
source: Time-lapse confocal microscopy revealed bright flashes of MS2cp signal in the ESC nucleus, which occurred in spatial proximity to the cuO and tetO labels
evidence: This is a direct observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: MS2 transcriptional bursts observed were similar to those observed elsewhere.
source: and were similar to the MS2 transcriptional bursts observed elsewhere (Bothma et al., 2014; Chubb et al., 2006; Lionnet et al., 2011; Martin et al., 2013; Ochiai et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature (Bothma et al., 2014; Chubb et al., 2006; Lionnet et al., 2011; Martin et al., 2013; Ochiai et al., 2014).

claim: The Sox2 MS2 reporter allele enables visualization of Sox2 transcription.
source: These results suggested the Sox2 MS2 reporter allele enables visualization of Sox2 transcription.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation of MS2 signal in proximity to the Sox2 locus.

claim: A total of 603 individual bursts were identified across 1,208 cells.
source: Using our pipeline, we identified a total of 603 individual bursts across 1,208 cells (Figure 5B, Supplementary files 5,6, Video 3)
evidence: This is based on automated analysis of the imaging data.

claim: Sox2 transcriptional activity is sporadic both between cells and within individual cells across time.
source: We found Sox2 transcriptional activity to be sporadic both between cells and within individual cells across time (Figure 5C)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: 66.1% of nuclei lacked detectable Sox2 transcription during the 30 min imaging window.
source: Nearly two-thirds (66.1%) of nuclei lacked detectable Sox2 transcription during our 30 min imaging window
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data.

claim: 29.3% of cells demonstrated transcriptional activity in less than 20% of frames.
source: with the majority of remaining cells demonstrating transcriptional activity in less than 20% of frames (29.3%, Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: 0.25% of cells demonstrated robust transcriptional activity in greater than half the observed frames.
source: However, we did observe rare cells that demonstrated robust transcriptional activity in greater than half the observed frames (0.25% of cells, Video 4)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data shown in Video 4.

claim: Substantial variability was found in the intensity of transcriptional bursts and their duration.
source: We also found substantial variability in the intensity of transcriptional bursts and their duration (Figure 5D)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Sox2-MS2 ESCs spent 4% of their time with a detectable MS2 burst.
source: As a population, we found Sox2-MS2 ESCs spent 4% of their time with a detectable MS2 burst (Figure 5E)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Live-cell measurements of Sox2 transcription suggest short, intermittent transcriptional activity in ESCs.
source: Thus, our live-cell measurements of Sox2transcription suggest short, intermittent transcriptional activity in ESCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of transcriptional bursts.

claim: Bursting frequency was significantly reduced in ESCs that expressed the MS2 coat protein but lacked the Sox2-MS2 reporter allele.
source: First, we measured bursting frequency in ESCs that expressed the MS2 coat protein but lacked the Sox2-MS2 reporter allele(Sox2-8CcuO/+, Sox2-117TtetO/+, Sox2WT/WT). ... In each case, we observed a significant drop in Sox2 burst frequency (Figure 5E)
evidence: This is based on comparison of bursting frequency shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Bursting frequency was significantly reduced in Sox2-MS2 ESCs that harbored an SCR deletion in cis.
source: Second, we measured bursting frequency in Sox2-MS2 ESCs that harbored an SCR deletion in cis (Sox2-8CcuO/+, Sox2-117TtetO/+, Sox2MS/WT, SCRdel/+). ... In each case, we observed a significant drop in Sox2 burst frequency (Figure 5E)
evidence: This is based on comparison of bursting frequency shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Bursting frequency was significantly reduced in Sox2-MS2 ESCs that were treated with the transcriptional inhibitor DRB.
source: Third, we measured bursting frequency in Sox2-MS2 ESCs that were treated with the transcriptional inhibitor 5,6-Dichloro-1-β-D-ribofuranosylbenzimidazole (DRB). In each case, we observed a significant drop in Sox2 burst frequency (Figure 5E)
evidence: This is based on comparison of bursting frequency shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The MS2 reporter cell line can accurately identify Sox2 transcriptional events.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate our ability to accurately identify Sox2 transcriptional events using our MS2 reporter cell line.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the control experiments showing reduced bursting in negative controls.

claim: Some transcriptionally active cells showed prolonged proximity of the Sox2/SCR labels.
source: We identified some transcriptionally active cells that showed prolonged proximity of the Sox2/SCR labels.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the imaging data.

claim: Cells were observed which showed robust transcriptional bursting despite a prolonged extended conformation of the Sox2 region.
source: However, we also observed cells which showed robust transcriptional bursting despite a prolonged extended conformation of the Sox2 region, driving Sox2/SCR distance above the population average for the duration of our 30 min imaging window (Figure 6B, Video 5)
evidence: This is a direct observation from the imaging data shown in Figure 6B and Video 5.

claim: All distance bins showed similar transcriptional activity.
source: We binned time points according to the measured distance between Sox2 and SCR and calculated the percent time spent bursting for each bin and found that all bins showed similar transcriptional activity (Figure 6C)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the imaging data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: No significant differences were found between bursting and non-bursting frames when segregating time points.
source: Furthermore, segregating time points into bursting and non-bursting frames for each cell demonstrated no significant differences between the two groups (Figure 6D, Mann-Whitney, p=0.68)
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis shown in Figure 6D (Mann-Whitney, p=0.68).

claim: Alignment and meta-analysis of bursts showed little change in Sox2/SCR distance across the time window.
source: Alignment and meta-analysis of these bursts showed little change in Sox2/SCR distance across the time window.
evidence: This is based on analysis of aligned burst data.

claim: No significant differences were found between burst-centered and random-centered analysis of Sox2/SCR distance.
source: To determine if Sox2/SCR distance significantly deviated from expected values across transcriptional bursts, we compared aligned bursts to a randomly shuffled control dataset and found no significant differences between the burst-centered and random-centered analysis (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 7)
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Sox2/SCR proximity and Sox2 transcription is not separated by a characteristic lag within the time frame considered.
source: This analysis suggests Sox2/SCR proximity and Sox2 transcription is not separated by a characteristic lag within the time frame considered.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the aligned burst analysis.

claim: Non-transcribing cells showed no correlation between order and distance.
source: As expected, non-transcribing cells showed no correlation between order and distance, given the ordering within this group was essentially random (Spearman's ρ = −0.01)
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis (Spearman's ρ = −0.01).

claim: Transcribing cells showed no correlation between transcriptional activity and distance.
source: However, transcribing cells also showed no correlation between transcriptional activity and distance (Spearman's ρ = 0.06)
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis (Spearman's ρ = 0.06).

claim: Transcribing cells demonstrated no significant difference in mean Sox2/SCR separation distance compared to non-transcribing cells.
source: As a group, transcribing cells demonstrated no significant difference in mean Sox2/SCR separation distance compared to non-transcribing cells (Figure 6G, Mann-Whitney, p=0.15)
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison shown in Figure 6G (Mann-Whitney, p=0.15).

claim: There is little relation between the 3D conformation of Sox2 relative to the SCR enhancer and its transcriptional output.
source: These data suggest little relation between the 3D conformation of Sox2 relative to the SCR enhancer and its transcriptional output.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lack of correlation between distance and transcription.

claim: SCR is unlikely to directly activate Sox2 transcription through contact with its promoter.
source: Thus, our data indicate SCR is unlikely to directly activate Sox2 transcription through contact with its promoter.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lack of association between Sox2/SCR proximity and transcription.

claim: Few unique spatial characteristics were observed for Sox2/SCR in ESCs.
source: We have investigated the dynamic 3D organization and underlying transcriptional activity of the established enhancer-gene pair Sox2 and SCR. Interestingly, we observe few unique spatial characteristics for Sox2/SCR in ESCs
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the distance measurements.

claim: Observed distance distributions and spatial dynamics for SCR and the Sox2 promoter region are similar to those observed between SCR and an equally-spaced non-specific region.
source: observed distance distributions and their spatial dynamics for SCR and the Sox2 promoter region are similar to those observed between SCR and an equally-spaced non-specific region.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the distance measurements.

claim: 3C-based assays have identified enriched contacts between Sox2/SCR as compared to the surrounding neighborhood.
source: In contrast, 3C-based assays have identified enriched contacts between Sox2/SCR as compared to the surrounding neighborhood.
evidence: This is stated as a contrast to the microscopy findings.

claim: Proximity ligation (3C) and separation distance (microscopy) are distinct measures of chromatin structure with unique biases, assumptions, and limitations.
source: We note that these results need not be incompatible. Proximity ligation (3C) and separation distance (microscopy) are distinct measures of chromatin structure with unique biases, assumptions, and limitations, and thus provide snapshots of chromatin architecture that may differ (Dekker, 2016; Fudenberg and Imakaev, 2017; Giorgetti and Heard, 2016)
evidence: This is a discussion point supported by citations (Dekker, 2016; Fudenberg and Imakaev, 2017; Giorgetti and Heard, 2016).

claim: 3C-based assays may capture rare conformations in the cell population that would have minimal impact on overall distance distributions constructed using microscopy.
source: 3C-based assays often utilize millions of cells and so may capture rare conformations in the cell population; these rare conformations would have minimal impact on overall distance distributions constructed using microscopy.
evidence: This is a speculation about the differences between 3C and microscopy.

claim: It remains unclear what spatial proximity is required to enable ligation events during 3C.
source: Moreover, it remains unclear what spatial proximity is required to enable ligation events during 3C, and this property may differ for distinct genomic regions.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of current knowledge.

claim: Enrichment of Sox2/SCR contacts in 3C assays may reflect only subtle differences in very proximal conformations (e.g. < 50 nm).
source: Indeed, enrichment of Sox2/SCR contacts in 3C assays may reflect only subtle differences in very proximal conformations (e.g. < 50 nm), conformations unlikely to be accurately represented by our microscopy measurements due to technical limitations in localization precision and uncertainty.
evidence: This is a speculation about the interpretation of the results.

claim: Large macromolecular bridges or hubs may enable crosslinking and ligation over larger distances that need not demonstrate pronounced spatial proximity.
source: Alternatively, large macromolecular bridges or hubs may enable crosslinking and ligation over larger distances that need not demonstrate pronounced spatial proximity, as recently demonstrated (Quinodoz et al., 2018)
evidence: This is a speculation supported by a citation (Quinodoz et al., 2018).

claim: A prolonged, proximal conformation established by stable, direct pairing of the Sox2 promoter with SCR is unlikely to be the predominant structure in ESCs.
source: For instance, the absence of enhanced proximity between the Sox2 and SCR pair suggests a prolonged, proximal conformation established by stable, direct pairing of the Sox2 promoter with SCR is unlikely to be the predominant structure in ESCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lack of enhanced proximity.

claim: No association was observed between Sox2/SCR proximity and Sox2 transcription in real time.
source: Surprisingly, we also observe no association between Sox2/SCR proximity and Sox2 transcription in real time.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the transcription analysis.

claim: No correlation was detected between transcriptional activity and instantaneous Sox2/SCR distances.
source: Indeed, we detect no correlation between transcriptional activity and instantaneous Sox2/SCR distances
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the transcription analysis.

claim: No reduction in Sox2/SCR distances was observed prior to transcriptional bursts.
source: no reduction in Sox2/SCR distances prior to transcriptional bursts
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the transcription analysis.

claim: No tendency for transcriptionally active cells to display reduced Sox2/SCR distance was observed.
source: and no tendency for transcriptionally active cells to display reduced Sox2/SCR distance.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the transcription analysis.

claim: Direct Sox2/SCR contacts may lead to a complex, multi-step activation process with stochastic delays between steps.
source: It is important to note that we cannot exclude the importance of direct Sox2/SCR contacts in Sox2 activation. If these events lead to a complex, multi-step activation process with stochastic delays between steps, it is plausible that enhancer-promoter contact and transcriptional output could be temporally decoupled and demonstrate the poor correlation between Sox2/SCR proximity and transcriptional activity that we observe.
evidence: This is a speculation about alternative interpretations of the results.

claim: Long-lived activation might be achieved through delivery of durable factors (e.g. chromatin modifiers) to the Sox2 promoter during contact.
source: This mechanism might be achieved through delivery of durable factors (e.g. chromatin modifiers) to the Sox2 promoter during contact
evidence: This is a speculation about a possible mechanism.

claim: Disruption of DNA loops genome-wide through acute RAD21 degradation leads to only modest changes in nascent transcription after 6 hr.
source: and might explain why disruption of DNA loops genome-wide through acute RAD21 degradation leads to only modest changes in nascent transcription after 6 hr (Rao et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by a citation (Rao et al., 2017).

claim: The Sox2 locus displays distinct behavior from an enhancer reporter recently used to explore the regulatory logic of the even-skipped (eve) enhancers in Drosophila embryos.
source: The Sox2 locus displays distinct behavior from an enhancer reporter recently used to explore the regulatory logic of the even-skipped (eve) enhancers in Drosophila embryos.
evidence: This is a comparison to another study.

claim: In the Drosophila eve system, the authors observe both bimodality in distance measurements as well as clear correlation between enhancer-reporter proximity and reporter transcription.
source: In this study, the authors integrated an enhancer reporter ~ 142 kb upstream of eve locus and promoted pairing between the two loci by including an ectopic insulator sequence, which pairs with a similar sequence embedded near the eve enhancers. In this system, the authors observe both bimodality in distance measurements as well as clear correlation between enhancer-reporter proximity and reporter transcription.
evidence: This is a description of findings from another study.

claim: There are considerable differences in the 3D distances reported for Sox2 (339 nm for Sox2/SCR) and those reported for the even-skipped reporter (709 nm for unpaired and 353 nm for paired).
source: While it is not yet clear why these systems behave so differently, we note the considerable differences in the 3D distances we report for Sox2 (339 nm for Sox2/SCR) and those reported for the even-skipped reporter (709 nm for unpaired and 353 nm for paired).
evidence: This is a comparison of distance measurements between studies.

claim: The more extended conformation of the Drosophila chromosome may necessitate pairing in order to bring the eve enhancer sufficiently close the reporter.
source: It seems plausible that the more extended conformation of the Drosophila chromosome necessitates pairing in order to bring the eve enhancer sufficiently close the reporter, particularly for enhancers evolved to function within 10 kb of their target gene.
evidence: This is a speculation about the differences between systems.

claim: Most Sox2/SCR loci reside within a distance range that may lower the importance of locus conformation for SCR function.
source: Our analysis suggests that most Sox2/SCR loci reside within this distance range, perhaps lowering the importance of locus conformation for SCR function.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the distance measurements.

claim: SCR transcriptional control demonstrates proximity dependence on some scale, as SCR ablation is not compensated for by a normal copy located on the homologous chromosome.
source: Indeed, SCR transcriptional control does demonstrate proximity dependence on some scale, as SCR ablation is not compensated for by a normal copy located on the homologous chromosome (Li et al., 2014; Zhou et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations (Li et al., 2014; Zhou et al., 2014).

claim: In contexts such as olfactory receptor gene choice or transvection in Drosophila, regulation can occur over very large distances in cis (~80 Mb) or in trans.
source: In other contexts, such as during olfactory receptor gene choice or transvection in Drosophila, regulation can occur over very large distances in cis (~80 Mb) or in trans
evidence: This is stated as a contrast to the Sox2 system.

claim: In olfactory receptor gene choice or transvection in Drosophila, transcriptional activity may be more closely tied to pairing events that promote spatial proximity.
source: and transcriptional activity may be more closely tied to pairing events that promote spatial proximity, as recently demonstrated for the latter (Horta et al., 2018; Lim et al., 2018; Markenscoff-Papadimitriou et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations (Horta et al., 2018; Lim et al., 2018; Markenscoff-Papadimitriou et al., 2014).

claim: Genomic interactions and other features of genome topology may differ in importance depending on the spatial distances navigated by enhancer-gene pairs.
source: Hence, genomic interactions and other features of genome topology may differ in importance depending of the spatial distances navigated by enhancer-gene pairs.
evidence: This is a speculation about the general principles of enhancer function.

claim: Direct contacts between Sox2 and SCR may be dispensable for SCR function.
source: Our observations also open the possibility that direct contacts between Sox2 and SCR are dispensable for SCR function.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the lack of association between proximity and transcription.

claim: SCR may play a critical role in the nucleation and spreading of important epigenetic activators and chromatin accessibility.
source: For example, SCR may play a critical role in the nucleation and spreading of important epigenetic activators and chromatin accessibility, establishing a permissive environment of Sox2 transcription.
evidence: This is a speculation about a possible mechanism.

claim: SCR is a bona fide super-enhancer in ESCs.
source: SCR is a bona fide super-enhancer in ESCs (Whyte et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by a citation (Whyte et al., 2013).

claim: Super-enhancers are capable of nucleating large (>300 nm), phase-separated condensates of coactivators, chromatin regulators, and transcription complexes.
source: An intriguing mechanism for action at a distance comes from recent observations that super-enhancers are capable of nucleating large (>300 nm), phase-separated condensates of coactivators, chromatin regulators, and transcription complexes (Cho et al., 2018; Sabari et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citations (Cho et al., 2018; Sabari et al., 2018).

claim: SCR may deliver activation factors over hundreds of nanometers through inclusion of the Sox2 promoter into an activator hub or condensate.
source: Thus, SCR may deliver activation factors over hundreds of nanometers through inclusion of the Sox2 promoter into an activator hub or condensate (Figure 6H, bottom).
evidence: This is a speculation illustrated in Figure 6H.

claim: A mechanism involving activator hubs would present challenges for achieving precise transcriptional control, most notably how SCR selectivity for Sox2 activation is achieved.
source: Such a mechanism would present a number of challenges for achieving precise transcriptional control, most notably how SCR selectivity for Sox2 activation is achieved.
evidence: This is a speculation about the implications of the proposed mechanism.

claim: Future studies that couple visualization of the Sox2 locus with that of important molecular components of transcriptional activation are likely to be essential in decoding how the SCR element achieves tight expression control of Sox2.
source: Nevertheless, future studies that couple visualization of the Sox2 locus with that of important molecular components of transcriptional activation are likely to be essential in decoding how the SCR element achieves tight expression control of this essential pluripotency gene.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Coexpression of CymR-GFP and TetR-tdTom did not significantly alter Sox2 expression from the modified 129 allele.
source: We confirmed that coexpression of CymR-GFP and TetR-tdTom did not significantly alter Sox2 expression from the modified 129 allele by qPCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Coexpression of CymR-GFP and TetR-tdTom did not alter Sox2-SCR contacts by 4C.
source: and did not alter Sox2-SCR contacts by 4C (Figure 1—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is based on 4C data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: 84% of assembled tracks for cuO span the full time series (>75 frames).
source: 84% and 62% of our assembled tracks span the full time series (>75 frames) for cuO and tetO, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on analysis of tracking data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: 62% of assembled tracks for tetO span the full time series (>75 frames).
source: 84% and 62% of our assembled tracks span the full time series (>75 frames) for cuO and tetO, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on analysis of tracking data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.
